findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — The PR silently removes start/end/statsPeriod date filtering (serializer fields and the datetime__range filter), so clients asking for a date range now get unfiltered audit logs with no error, which contradicts the "performance" framing.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime (key is "datetime"), so build_cursor raises TypeError and every non-empty optimized_pagination=true request returns a 500.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, and build_queryset compares it to the datetime column (`datetime <= <int>`), so any valued cursor (including DateTimePaginator ms-timestamp cursors) causes a DB type error or wrong filtering.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — enable_advanced runs on every request even when optimized_pagination is not requested, and it dereferences organization_context.member, which is None for non-superuser callers without membership (e.g. API-key or token auth), raising AttributeError and a 500 on the default path.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The "advanced" negative-offset branch passes a user-controlled negative start to a Django QuerySet slice, which raises "Negative indexing is not supported"; any admin can force a 500 with ?cursor=0:-N:0, and the comments saying "Django handles negative slicing" and "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" are false and describe an unsafe intent.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The BasePaginator change affects every paginated endpoint in Sentry: it still passes negative offsets through unclamped when is_prev=1, so ?cursor=X:-N:1 still 500s everywhere while the comment says "safe"; it also silently clamps negative offsets for next cursors instead of rejecting them.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The gate uses the raw request.user.is_superuser flag instead of is_active_superuser(request), and has_global_access is true for every member of an open-membership org, so the "authorized administrators only" gate is much weaker than it claims.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:886 — For is_prev cursors the "advanced" and normal branches run the same unclamped slice, so the admin gate does not actually decide whether negative offsets reach the ORM.

src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The added comment says Cursor "allows negative offsets" but no validation or bounds handling was added, so crafted negative offsets are documented as supported yet crash downstream paginators.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod from the audit-logs query serializer silently breaks existing callers: DRF ignores unknown params, so clients asking for a date range now get unfiltered results instead of an error.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator uses a different cursor value format from DateTimePaginator (raw value instead of epoch-ms converted to datetime; floor/ceil on a datetime), so cursors in the Link header are not interchangeable between the two modes of the same endpoint and the optimized path breaks on datetime keys.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — Client-supplied negative cursor offsets are passed straight to the queryset slice, creating a new cursor contract that is unsupported (Django rejects negative indexing, so the request returns a 500) and exposing results outside the normal pagination window.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — This shared BasePaginator change alters the cursor contract for every endpoint: a negative offset on a next cursor is now silently clamped to 0 instead of rejected, while a negative offset on a prev cursor still reaches the slice, so behavior differs by direction.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — The new optimized_pagination query param is undocumented, is not declared in the query serializer, and is silently ignored for non-admin callers, so the same request gets different pagination and cursor semantics depending on who sends it.

src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The comment says negative offsets are now officially allowed, but Cursor/from_string has no validation or documented contract, so API consumers can't tell whether negative cursor offsets are supported input.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to the `datetime` attribute, so any non-empty page raises TypeError inside build_cursor, which makes the optimized path return 500.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — enable_advanced` runs on every request, including the default path, and dereferences `organization_context.member`; that is None for non-member callers (staff, org auth tokens, non-superuser admins), so the endpoint raises AttributeError and returns 500.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:23 — The start/end/statsPeriod serializer fields and the datetime__range filter were removed, so date-filtered requests are silently ignored and return unfiltered audit logs (a behavioral regression).

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — The negative-offset "advanced" branch slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start; Django raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so the feature always fails with 500 instead of paginating.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset then compares against the DateTimeField `datetime`, so any cursor with a value fails or filters wrongly (unlike DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion).

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — A negative offset on a forward cursor is clamped to 0 for the slice, but build_cursor still uses the raw negative cursor.offset for next/prev offsets, which produces inconsistent follow-up cursors that repeat rows.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result (with its explanatory comments stripped), so fixes to the base will drift from this copy.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The enable_advanced_features branch and the else branch run the same slice logic (the else branch already passes negative offsets through for is_prev), so the flag is a redundant, confusing code path.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — get_item_key/value_from_cursor are copied from the numeric Paginator but the class is wired to order_by="-datetime", so math.floor on a datetime crosses a type boundary (TypeError) and it duplicates Paginator instead of reusing DateTimePaginator.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876 — The comments claiming "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" are wrong (Django rejects negative indexing) and hide the real risk.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The shared BasePaginator slicing now handles offsets asymmetrically (clamps them for next, passes negatives for prev), which changes every paginator subclass with no stated reason, and the "safe because the queryset will handle boundary conditions" comment is misleading.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:822 — The docstring advertises an "optimized query path" and "streamlined boundary handling" that the code does not implement; the endpoint comments at organization_auditlogs.py:68-75 make the same unsupported claims.
src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — This comment describes a "performance optimization" that has no matching code change, so it misleads readers about what Cursor does.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:25 — The PR silently removes the start/end/statsPeriod date filters (and the get_date_range_from_stats_period import), an unrelated API behavior change outside the stated pagination scope.
src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:76 — The two self.paginate calls are duplicates that differ only in paginator_cls plus one kwarg; they should build the paginator args once.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:82 — The endpoint passes the paginator-internal flag enable_advanced_features=True after already gating on permissions, which leaks paginator internals into the endpoint and double-gates the same behavior.
src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:72 — Trailing whitespace on line 72 and after order_by="-datetime", on line 89.
src/sentry/api/paginator.py:824 — Trailing whitespace in the OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring (lines 824, 827, 829).
src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820 — Three blank lines before the class (PEP 8 expects two) and a trailing blank line at end of file (line 912).
src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:23 — A stray blank line was added directly after the AuditLogQueryParamSerializer class declaration.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod date-range filtering means every audit-log request scans the org's full history and client-supplied date bounds are silently ignored, which widens the scan on high-volume orgs.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:878 — OptimizedCursorPaginator is a copy of BasePaginator.get_result using the same build_queryset plus OFFSET/LIMIT slicing, so it gives no measurable gain over DateTimePaginator (no keyset seek, no count avoidance) despite its "optimized" name.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — Negative-offset slicing of a Django QuerySet is not "handled automatically": the ORM raises on negative indexes, and emulating it would need a full count or materialization, so this path cannot give efficient reverse pagination.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:884 — The new paginator applies no max_offset cap on the client-controlled cursor offset, so crafted cursors can force deep OFFSET scans (made worse by the removed date filter).

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — A user-supplied negative cursor offset slices the QuerySet with a negative index, which Django rejects with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") and returns an unhandled 500.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the datetime `datetime` field, which raises TypeError in build_cursor on every non-empty optimized page and returns a 500.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, and build_queryset compares that integer against the timestamp `datetime` column, which causes a DB type error (500) or wrong filtering on any cursor with a value.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member.has_global_access` runs on every request even without optimized_pagination, so a non-superuser caller with no member (e.g. API key or token auth) hits AttributeError on None and gets a 500 on the normal path.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The shared BasePaginator still passes negative offsets through unvalidated for is_prev cursors (e.g. `0:-5:1`), so Django raises ValueError and every endpoint using Paginator/DateTimePaginator returns a 500 instead of a 400.

src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:28 — Cursor accepts any negative offset from untrusted input with no validation or BadPaginationError, so the error surfaces later as a 500 instead of being rejected as a 400.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removing the start/end/statsPeriod filters silently drops date-range bounding, so audit log queries on high-volume orgs scan unbounded ranges, which risks slow queries or timeouts.
src/sentry/api/paginator.py:890 — With a negative offset, the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` trim check can never match, so the prev-page trimming breaks and returns extra or wrong rows.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The privilege gate checks raw request.user.is_superuser instead of is_active_superuser(request), so a superuser flag with no active sudo session unlocks the advanced paginator.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — has_global_access is not an admin check (every member of an open-membership org has it), so ordinary members can turn on the "admin-only" negative-offset paginator just by adding ?optimized_pagination=true.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member can be None for callers that are not members (e.g. org-level tokens or staff), so this line throws AttributeError and returns a 500 instead of failing closed.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:879 — The comment claiming "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" is misleading, because it treats deliberately out-of-bounds slicing as harmless and hides the unvalidated user input.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Shared BasePaginator (used by every endpoint) still passes a user-supplied negative offset unclamped when is_prev=1, under a false "this is safe" comment, where it should reject negative offsets outright.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator has zero tests, and any test would catch that get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the datetime key and raises TypeError for every non-empty optimized_pagination=true response.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now slices with a negative offset when is_prev is set, which changes behavior for every paginator subclass, and there is no test for negative-offset prev cursors (Django rejects negative slicing and returns a 500).

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The negative-offset "advanced" branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator is untested; a cursor like 0:-10:0 would crash on Django's negative-indexing assertion or expose out-of-bounds rows.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removing the start/end/statsPeriod params and datetime__range filtering is a silent API break with no test changes, so existing date-filter endpoint tests will now fail because filters are ignored.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — No test covers a non-superuser caller whose organization_context.member is None (e.g. token or staff access), where .has_global_access raises AttributeError and returns a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — The PR silently removes start/end/statsPeriod date filtering (serializer fields and the datetime__range filter), so clients asking for a date range now get unfiltered audit logs with no error, which contradicts the "performance" framing.

adjudication.rationale: The shown diff in `organization_auditlogs.py` only changes pagination behavior (imports `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, adds an `optimized_pagination` flag, and chooses between `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `DateTimePaginator`). There are no changes in the displayed diff removing start/end/statsPeriod serializer fields or removing a `datetime__range` filter; no date-range filtering code is deleted or altered here. Therefore the claim that the PR “silently removes” date filtering is not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime (key is "datetime"), so build_cursor raises TypeError and every non-empty optimized_pagination=true request returns a 500.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, and build_queryset compares it to the datetime column (`datetime <= <int>`), so any valued cursor (including DateTimePaginator ms-timestamp cursors) causes a DB type error or wrong filtering.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is now selectable for the audit log endpoint, which orders by the `datetime` field (`order_by="-datetime"`). However, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor()` just returns `cursor.value` unchanged, and `get_item_key()` treats the field value as numeric (`math.floor/ceil` and `int(...)`). Nothing in the diff shows conversion from a cursor representation (e.g., a timestamp integer) into a `datetime`, so using this paginator against a datetime-ordered queryset is very likely to produce incorrect comparisons/filters (or DB type errors) when `build_queryset(...)` applies the cursor value to the `datetime` column. This mismatch is directly introduced by wiring `OptimizedCursorPaginator` into `organization_auditlogs.py`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — enable_advanced runs on every request even when optimized_pagination is not requested, and it dereferences organization_context.member, which is None for non-superuser callers without membership (e.g. API-key or token auth), raising AttributeError and a 500 on the default path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `enable_advanced` is computed on every request (`enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`) before the `if use_optimized and enable_advanced:` gate, so any `organization_context.member` nullability would affect even the default (non-optimized) path. However, the diff alone does not establish that `organization_context.member` can be `None` for callers reaching this endpoint (it may be guaranteed by auth/permission layers not shown), so the claimed 500/AttributeError is not fully verifiable from the diff. It is still a concrete, diff-grounded robustness issue: the new code introduces an unconditional dereference that could crash if `member` is absent, and it should be short-circuited/guarded by `use_optimized` or a `member is not None` check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The "advanced" negative-offset branch passes a user-controlled negative start to a Django QuerySet slice, which raises "Negative indexing is not supported"; any admin can force a 500 with ?cursor=0:-N:0, and the comments saying "Django handles negative slicing" and "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" are false and describe an unsafe intent.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The BasePaginator change affects every paginated endpoint in Sentry: it still passes negative offsets through unclamped when is_prev=1, so ?cursor=X:-N:1 still 500s everywhere while the comment says "safe"; it also silently clamps negative offsets for next cursors instead of rejecting them.

adjudication.rationale: The BasePaginator.get_result change sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. This means negative `cursor.offset` values are still passed through unchanged when `cursor.is_prev` is true, while they are clamped to 0 for non-prev cursors. The diff introduces no validation/rejection for negative offsets on the prev path, despite comments claiming safety; a negative queryset slice start is not handled here and can still raise (500).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The gate uses the raw request.user.is_superuser flag instead of is_active_superuser(request), and has_global_access is true for every member of an open-membership org, so the "authorized administrators only" gate is much weaker than it claims.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff clearly introduces a new gate in `organization_auditlogs.py`:
```py
enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access
```
while the surrounding comments claim “authorized administrators only.” The finding’s specific assertion that it should use `is_active_superuser(request)` and that `has_global_access` is true for every member of an open-membership org is not verifiable from this diff alone, but the mismatch between the stated intent (admins only) and the broad-looking predicate (`has_global_access`) is a concrete review concern grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:886 — For is_prev cursors the "advanced" and normal branches run the same unclamped slice, so the admin gate does not actually decide whether negative offsets reach the ORM.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the non-advanced branch sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so when `cursor.is_prev` is true it uses `offset` unclamped. That means a negative `cursor.offset` will reach `queryset[start_offset:stop]` even when `enable_advanced_features` is false, making the advanced/admin gate ineffective for `is_prev` cursors. The earlier change in `DateTimePaginator.get_result` has the same unclamped `is_prev` behavior. This is a real behavioral defect introduced by the diff (and can also trigger Django QuerySet negative-slice errors).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The added comment says Cursor "allows negative offsets" but no validation or bounds handling was added, so crafted negative offsets are documented as supported yet crash downstream paginators.

adjudication.rationale: The diff newly documents negative offsets in `Cursor` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py) and adds code paths that may actually pass negative offsets into queryset slicing: in `BasePaginator.get_result` it uses `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset` (so a negative `cursor.offset` with `is_prev=True` is not clamped), and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`. There is no validation/bounds handling added to ensure negative offsets are safe, so a crafted cursor with negative offset can lead to runtime errors in downstream pagination/query slicing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod from the audit-logs query serializer silently breaks existing callers: DRF ignores unknown params, so clients asking for a date range now get unfiltered results instead of an error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes pagination behavior in `organization_auditlogs.py` (adding `optimized_pagination` flag and choosing between `DateTimePaginator` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator`) and adds/adjusts paginator/cursor offset handling. There is no change shown that removes `start`, `end`, or `statsPeriod` from any audit-logs query serializer or alters date-range filtering/validation, so the finding is not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator uses a different cursor value format from DateTimePaginator (raw value instead of epoch-ms converted to datetime; floor/ceil on a datetime), so cursors in the Link header are not interchangeable between the two modes of the same endpoint and the optimized path breaks on datetime keys.

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint now conditionally paginates the same `queryset` ordered by `-datetime` using either `DateTimePaginator` or the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()`, it does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor/ceil(value)` before casting to `int`, which will raise a `TypeError` if `self.key` is a `datetime` (as implied by `order_by="-datetime"`). Additionally, `value_from_cursor()` returns the raw `cursor.value` with no datetime/epoch conversion, so cursors generated in one mode are unlikely to be usable in the other mode for the same endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — Client-supplied negative cursor offsets are passed straight to the queryset slice, creating a new cursor contract that is unsupported (Django rejects negative indexing, so the request returns a 500) and exposing results outside the normal pagination window.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly enables negative offsets to reach the queryset slice. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Additionally, the earlier change in `paginator.py` uses `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which can also pass a negative `offset` through when `cursor.is_prev` is true. The `Cursor` class now comments about allowing negative offsets and still assigns `self.offset = int(offset)` with no validation, so a client-supplied cursor can carry a negative offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and will raise an error, leading to a 500, and it also changes the cursor contract by allowing offsets outside the normal window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — This shared BasePaginator change alters the cursor contract for every endpoint: a negative offset on a next cursor is now silently clamped to 0 instead of rejected, while a negative offset on a prev cursor still reaches the slice, so behavior differs by direction.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the shared `BasePaginator.get_result` slice start was changed from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. This means a negative `cursor.offset` on a forward/next page (`cursor.is_prev == False`) is silently clamped to 0, while a negative offset on a prev page still flows into the slice unmodified. This is a real behavior change and creates direction-dependent handling of invalid/negative offsets across all endpoints using this paginator (and may still error for prev cursors).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — The new optimized_pagination query param is undocumented, is not declared in the query serializer, and is silently ignored for non-admin callers, so the same request gets different pagination and cursor semantics depending on who sends it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `optimized_pagination` switch read directly from `request.GET` (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) and gates it on `is_superuser` / `has_global_access`. For non-admins the param is silently ignored and the endpoint falls back to `DateTimePaginator`, while admins get `OptimizedCursorPaginator` plus `enable_advanced_features=True`, so the same request (including the query param) can produce different pagination/cursor behavior depending on caller privileges. The diff does not show this param being part of the existing validated `query` filter params flow, which is a concrete review issue even if intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The comment says negative offsets are now officially allowed, but Cursor/from_string has no validation or documented contract, so API consumers can't tell whether negative cursor offsets are supported input.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds a comment in `Cursor.__init__` about negative offsets and does not show `Cursor.from_string` (or any parsing/validation/contract documentation) being missing or incorrect. Since the finding hinges on behavior and documentation not present in the diff, it can’t be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to the `datetime` attribute, so any non-empty page raises TypeError inside build_cursor, which makes the optimized path return 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset then compares against the DateTimeField `datetime`, so any cursor with a value fails or filters wrongly (unlike DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — A negative offset on a forward cursor is clamped to 0 for the slice, but build_cursor still uses the raw negative cursor.offset for next/prev offsets, which produces inconsistent follow-up cursors that repeat rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` `BasePaginator.get_result`, the new logic sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so when `cursor.is_prev` is true a user-controlled `cursor.offset` can be negative and is passed directly into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. The diff also updates `Cursor.offset = int(offset)` with an explicit comment about allowing negative offsets. Django QuerySet slicing does not safely support negative indexing/slicing and can raise errors, so this is a real broken-behavior risk in shared paginator code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator has zero tests, and any test would catch that get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the datetime key and raises TypeError for every non-empty optimized_pagination=true response.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` applies `math.floor/ceil` to `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and casts to `int`. In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized path paginates audit logs with `order_by="-datetime"`, which strongly implies the paginator key will be the `datetime` field. Applying `math.floor/ceil` to a `datetime` value would raise `TypeError`, breaking any non-empty `optimized_pagination=true` response for eligible users. The “zero tests” aspect is secondary; the core issue is a diff-introduced runtime error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now slices with a negative offset when is_prev is set, which changes behavior for every paginator subclass, and there is no test for negative-offset prev cursors (Django rejects negative slicing and returns a 500).

adjudication.rationale: In BasePaginator.get_result the diff changes slicing to clamp offsets to >=0 only when NOT cursor.is_prev (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). For `is_prev=True`, it still uses `offset` exactly as before (`queryset[offset:stop]`), so the diff does not newly introduce negative-offset slicing for prev cursors nor change behavior for every subclass in that way. The finding’s claim is therefore a misread of the shown change (though the new OptimizedCursorPaginator does introduce optional negative-offset slicing, that’s not what the finding asserts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The negative-offset "advanced" branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator is untested; a cursor like 0:-10:0 would crash on Django's negative-indexing assertion or expose out-of-bounds rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the “advanced” branch explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative slice indices (they assert on negative indexing), so a cursor producing a negative offset (e.g. `0:-10:0`) would likely raise an exception at runtime. This defective behavior is introduced by the new negative-offset branch; whether it is tested is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removing the start/end/statsPeriod params and datetime__range filtering is a silent API break with no test changes, so existing date-filter endpoint tests will now fail because filters are ignored.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove handling of start/end/statsPeriod params nor any `datetime__range` filtering in `organization_auditlogs.py`. The only endpoint change shown is swapping between `DateTimePaginator` and a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` based on `optimized_pagination` and admin access. No date-filter logic is deleted or modified in the provided hunks, so the claim of silently breaking date filtering isn’t supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — No test covers a non-superuser caller whose organization_context.member is None (e.g. token or staff access), where .has_global_access raises AttributeError and returns a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`. If `organization_context.member` can ever be `None`, this new code path would raise `AttributeError` (500) when evaluating `.has_global_access`. The finding’s ask for a test (and implicitly a guard) is tied to this newly introduced conditional logic, but the diff alone doesn’t prove `member` is nullable in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — The permission gate for optimized_pagination has no tests showing that non-admin members fall back to DateTimePaginator while superusers and global-access members get the optimized path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new branching logic in `organization_auditlogs.py` choosing `OptimizedCursorPaginator` only when `optimized_pagination=true` and the user is a superuser or has `member.has_global_access`; otherwise it falls back to `DateTimePaginator`. No corresponding test changes are included in this diff to exercise/lock down the permission-gated behavior of this new branch, so the concern is specific to the added nontrivial logic even though it’s not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:891 — The is_prev trimming in OptimizedCursorPaginator compares against offset instead of start_offset and has no prev-page test with a cursor value to check for dropped or duplicated rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the `is_prev` trimming logic uses `offset` (`cursor.offset`) in `len(results) == offset + limit + extra`, but for `cursor.is_prev` the code always sets `start_offset = offset` (and in the advanced negative-offset branch `start_offset = cursor.offset` as well). So there is no diff-grounded mismatch of comparing against `offset` instead of `start_offset`. The claim about lacking a prev-page test is also not verifiable from the diff (no tests are shown).
